title: Telling the Story
coreMove: Compress the pitch into a sequence of change, stakes, and point so the room can follow without drowning in detail.
sourcePressure: Story chapter: a pitch story transfers meaning quickly and guides attention without rambling, front-loading history, or replacing substance with autobiography.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must make story a compressed meaning-transfer tool, not a long origin tale or soft substitute for substance.

counterintuition: The point comes before the history

exampleSpecs.domain: marine salvage company pitching a rapid-response contract to a port insurer
exampleSpecs.audience: an operator with dramatic incidents but too much technical backstory
exampleSpecs.stakes: the insurer misses the value of hour-one mobilization after a container spill
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he starts with the first floating container at dawn, then moves straight to the decision clock instead of reciting company history
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wet orange towline coiled beside a tide-stained claim form

exampleSpecs.domain: chef-owner pitching a regional frozen-meal line to hospital dietitians
exampleSpecs.audience: a food entrepreneur tempted to tell a full restaurant backstory
exampleSpecs.stakes: dietitians need to see sodium control and patient uptake before they hear brand romance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she cuts the family-restaurant opening and begins with one patient tray returning empty after months of untouched meals
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a clean hospital tray beside a freezer-label proof

exampleSpecs.domain: subsea cable repair planner briefing an island utility board
exampleSpecs.audience: a planner whose chronology can sprawl across storms, ships, and permits
exampleSpecs.stakes: the board must approve pre-positioned repair gear before the next outage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he draws only three moments from the last outage, cable break, waiting vessel, dark clinic, and stops before the technical appendix
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a frayed cable cross-section inside a clear case

exampleSpecs.domain: independent game studio pitching a licensing partnership for an educational puzzle game
exampleSpecs.audience: a creative lead with lore, mechanics, and learning science competing for room
exampleSpecs.stakes: the licensor sees a toy instead of a repeatable learning loop
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she narrates one child failing a puzzle, changing one move, and asking for the next level before showing retention metrics
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a handheld controller resting on a printed level map

exampleSpecs.domain: forensic accounting firm pitching fraud detection to a family-owned manufacturer
exampleSpecs.audience: an accountant with too many audit steps in the opening
exampleSpecs.stakes: the owners tune out before seeing how one invoice pattern exposed a leak
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he shows three invoice dates and asks which one does not belong before revealing the month-end leakage pattern
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three invoice copies fanned across a walnut table

exampleSpecs.domain: reef restoration scientist pitching a tourism tax renewal to hotel managers
exampleSpecs.audience: a scientist who usually starts with species names and grant history
exampleSpecs.stakes: hotel managers need the visitor-economy sequence before the ecology details
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she opens with a snorkel guide refunding a disappointed family, then connects the lost booking to the reef nursery result
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a scratched snorkel mask beside a resort cancellation sheet

skillTargets: choose story beats that transfer meaning quickly
analyze whether a story guides attention or distracts
evaluate when narrative has replaced substance

tryThisNowSpec: Write your pitch story in four beats: moment, change, stakes, point. Delete any beat that only proves you worked hard.
